scope: Read-only static review of the BF16 supervisor, its fixture tests, and its production-shaped test source. No parser11-dependent test, production replay, admission, materialization, analyzer, build, or launch was invoked.

findings.detail: The real child dispatch path creates a ChildStage at supervisor-16 lines 940-946 and then enters the lossless runtime at lines 947-950, but it never calls bridge11.assert_child_ready or admission16.validate_child_stage. bridge11.assert_child_ready is the reviewed guard that checks the parent stage is still current, the child stage is current, and the startup lease remains positive (bridge11 lines 1864-1872); admission16.validate_child_stage is the corresponding admission boundary (admission16 lines 1178-1192). The supervisor's staged_child_ready helper exists at lines 1580-1594, but is called only by the synthetic tests. The child currently verifies compact parent identity, graph binding, lock, ledger, and lease through create_child_stage and validate_lease_progress; that is not an invocation of the explicit parent-current/child-ready guard and does not validate the parent's current stage sidecars through an opaque parent stage.
findings.impact: A stale or changed parent stage can pass the actual child path if its compact receipt and referenced ledger still match, while the reviewed child-ready API would reject it. The focused tests can pass because they call staged_child_ready directly and do not prove that run_groups/_run_frozen_group dispatch through the same guard. This leaves the production child admission boundary weaker than the advertised stage API.
findings.required_correction: Add a production-reachable, process-boundary-safe child-ready validation before executor.run_group. It must validate the exact parent and child stage/graph/lock/ledger bindings and positive startup lease, using the pinned bridge/admission instances; if the opaque parent cannot cross the process boundary, add an equivalent bridge API that validates the compact parent receipt and current parent sidecars without treating serialized diagnostics as runtime authority. Add an end-to-end fixture that proves the real _run_frozen_group path invokes this guard and rejects a stale parent/late phase. Keep the existing 120-second handshake, finite lease, source/resource guards, 21/20 cardinalities, and no-retry behavior unchanged.

findings.detail: The supervisor16 source retains stale provenance labels in the live diagnostic data and source-loader errors: PER_ATTEMPT_STARTUP_ALLOWANCE_SOURCE names replacement-07 (line 51), _load_module gives every loaded module a v092_replacement09_supervisor_* spec name (line 174), and admission/bridge error strings say canonical v07/v02 (lines 197 and 204). The actual path constants are BF16/bridge11 and the numeric startup allowance is guarded, so this is not treated as a guard bypass, but emitted provenance can misidentify the source of a live lease or failure.
findings.required_correction: Relabel these diagnostics to the exact BF16/bridge11 source identities or explicitly mark them as legacy compatibility labels, then bind the emitted value in the final packet. Do not change the numeric lease, resource policy, or frozen source guard as a workaround.

positive_static_evidence: The supervisor binds the current protocol16, admission16, bridge11, and supervisor16 paths and supplies the same four host graph roles at child and parent graph construction sites.

The child command has one Popen site, uses the captured popen monotonic origin, verifies the inherited canonical lock and PID/birth/argv permit, and restores executor contenders/lock/clock in a finally block.

The parent loop performs a stage-current check before each dispatch, charges command/admission/phase/wait work to one finite lease, creates exactly one successor per completed group, and has no retry branch.
The configuration CLI remains hard-rejected, so this review does not treat configuration as qualified by the batch path.
